CHIEF COMPLAINT
Status post mitral valve repair (performed 8/3/2020).

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is presenting for follow-up following mitral valve repair performed on 8/3/2020. At previous follow-up on 9/17, patient was doing well from a cardiac standpoint. Patient reports feeling better than before surgery and overall doing quite well. She continues to experience some chest pain and shallow breathing associated with exertion. Episodes are brief, lasting only a few minutes, and resolve with rest and reduced activity. When experiencing symptoms, patient slows down and takes it easy, after which she can usually resume activities. Episodes occur approximately a couple times per month with symptom-free intervals lasting a couple weeks. Patient is taking medications regularly with assistance from a reminder app. Patient has history of mitral regurgitation, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, asthma, and recurrent chest discomfort with previous negative workup for coronary artery disease.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies new symptoms. Continues to experience some chest pain and shallow breathing, typically associated with exertion. No medication side effects reported currently. Patient noted initial irritability with atenolol that has since resolved.

- Mitral valve repair (8/3/2020)
- Mitral regurgitation
- Atrial fibrillation
- Diabetes
- Asthma
- Recurrent chest discomfort with negative cardiac workup for coronary artery disease

MEDICATIONS

- Lasix 4 milligrams daily

RESULTS
ECG (today): Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response, well controlled with current medications.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Patient is recovering nicely from mitral valve repair with heart valves working well and functioning properly. Atrial fibrillation is well controlled with current medications. Continue current medications: Coumadin 4 mg, Lasix 4 mg daily, Atenolol 50 mg daily. Encourage patient to remain active as this will aid recovery. Follow-up appointment in 6-9 months.
